source.title: LC-PLM: Long-context Protein Language Modeling Using Bidirectional Mamba with Shared Projection Layers
source.authors: Ying-Heng Wang; Zi-Chen Wang; Gil Sadeh; L. Zancato; Alessandro Achille; George Karypis; H. Rangwala

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Measures held-out cross-entropy loss across model sizes, as in scaling-law studies, but applies this measurement to protein masked-language models and compares a different architecture.
record.gate_note: The parameter-scaling results in Figure 4 and the depth comparison in Figure 5 bear on the claim. Loss values for individual model sizes are shown only in figures and are not numerically transcribed in the provided text. Downstream-task scores, graph-context results, and structure-prediction scores do not measure the versions of the claim listed here.
record.test_reason: The study trains protein masked-language models (LC-PLM, BiMamba-S; ESM-2, Transformer) at four sizes on 20B UniRef90 tokens and plots held-out cross-entropy against parameter count (Sec. 5.1, Fig. 4). That is a new setting, protein sequences, for the loss-vs-size claim. Sec. 5.3 compares depth at a fixed 740M parameter count. No power law is fitted and the sweep spans about one order of magnitude, so this is T3 (new setting) rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors claim LC-PLM shows favourable scaling (sharper slope than ESM-2) and an average 13.5% lower evaluation loss at similar sizes. They attribute this to SSM long-range modelling and the deeper BiMamba-S design, and suggest stacking layers over widening at fixed parameters.
record.recipe_differences: Uses bidirectional Mamba with masked language modeling on protein sequences rather than the original natural-language scaling setup; varies parameter count at a fixed training amount and does not fit compute-optimal allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports a 4.5% evaluation-loss improvement for the deeper BiMamba-S architecture over BiMamba at the same stated parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: At similar sizes, the SSM architecture (LC-PLM) has 13.5% lower average evaluation loss than the Transformer (ESM-2) and a sharper loss-vs-size slope.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The scaling slope and offset depend on architecture family (SSM vs Transformer) in protein MLMs.

record.problems: The parameter sweep has four sizes per model, spans only 100M–1.3B for LC-PLM and 150M–1B for ESM-2, and holds the training amount fixed. No fitted exponents or numerical loss values for individual sizes are given in the text; those values are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on these claim versions were left out. Downstream-task, graph-context, and structure-prediction results were excluded because they do not measure the claimed scaling behavior.

untested.parts: No text-LM results. The protein results are recorded under V5.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep; tokens are held at 20B.
Width, aspect ratio across a wide range, and Transformer shape variation.
Token and compute scaling, fitted exponents, a multi-order-of-magnitude range, and other modalities and regimes (image, video, repeated data, fine-tuning).
Downstream scores are reported at one size per model, not as a function of scale or loss.
No comparison of fitting choices or of curve bending.

missing.what: Average 13.5% lower evaluation loss for LC-PLM vs ESM-2 at similar model sizes
Untied vs tied embeddings give better evaluation loss (no number given)

record.verdict_notes: bioRxiv/arXiv preprint by the model's developers; the scaling experiment is a secondary result. The rows were relinked from V1 to V5 because protein sequences are a non-text modality. No individual loss values or exponents are given in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Only parameter count is varied. Token- and compute-scaling, fitted exponents, and behavior across several orders of magnitude are not tested.
No power law fitted on small runs is used to predict the loss of larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token trend is tested.
The study compares depth at one stated parameter count; it does not test width or a wide range of architecture choices.
Tests protein-sequence masked-language modeling only; image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, and transfer regimes are not tested for scaling-law form.
Downstream task scores are reported, but the study does not test whether they improve predictably with scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or compute-optimal splits is reported, and no systematic test of curve bending is made.

rows.subject: LC-PLM-740M w/ BiMamba-S
rows.operation_detail: Compares evaluation loss against the 740M BiMamba model with half the depth.

conditions.value: BiMamba-S versus BiMamba with half the depth

rows.note: The paper states that the deeper BiMamba-S model improves evaluation loss by 4.5%; the comparison is at one parameter count and tests depth, not width or a broad architecture range.
rows.check: A 2x-depth change at fixed ~740M parameters shifts evaluation loss by 4.5%. That is modest but not negligible, and the authors present it as a meaningful gain. Depth is confounded with shared projection layers (BiMamba-S vs BiMamba). The model is an SSM, not a Transformer, trained on UniRef50 with the token count unstated. State 'partial' means 'shape matters little' holds only weakly here.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.3, Figure 5; Section 4.1, Shared Projection Layers.

relationships.condition: LC-PLM (BiMamba-S) protein MLM, 100M–1.3B params, 20B UniRef90 tokens
relationships.reason: Held-out loss is stated to fall with size (R1–R4), but only over ~1 order of magnitude at fixed tokens, with no power-law fit. The slope also differs by architecture (LC-PLM sharper than ESM-2), so the same form is shown only as a monotone trend.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out loss fell across roughly one order of magnitude in model size, more sharply than ESM-2, without a fitted power law.
